posts.title: Test AI phone agents with repeatable calls
posts.promise: Run a scripted call against a phone agent and receive a reviewable pass or fail result.
posts.whatItIs: VoiceGremlin is described by its maker as an API for testing AI systems that answer phone calls. A user supplies a phone number and a test case, such as checking whether the agent performs a requested behavior. The service calls the agent, has the two bots converse, and uses an LLM judge—a language model asked to assess the result—to return pass or fail for a software pipeline. A small student version could run one scripted scenario against a test phone agent and save the call outcome. Teams building voice agents are a plausible customer, but the source does not establish who pays or whether customers use it. The repeated loop can run without a person placing each test call, while a human still needs to configure safe test numbers, inspect ambiguous calls, and decide what failures mean.
posts.whoPays: Hypothesis: companies building AI phone agents may pay to check that their agents keep meeting defined behaviors; the source provides no customer or revenue evidence.
loop: An operator defines a test case and supplies a test phone number.
The API places a call to the phone agent being checked.
The test bot speaks with the phone agent about the scenario.
An LLM judge compares the conversation with the requested behavior.
The system returns a pass or fail result to a software pipeline.
A developer reviews unclear failures and updates the test or phone agent.
posts.evidence: In a Show HN post, the maker says VoiceGremlin is a working API for tests against AI phone agents: a user supplies a phone number and test case, the service has bots converse, and an LLM judge provides a pass/fail result for a pipeline. The maker also describes a free trial. These are maker statements, not independent reliability or adoption evidence.
posts.uncertainty: The source is the founder's description and provides no independent accuracy results. LLM judgements can misread a conversation, and a test call can incur telephony costs or reach an unintended person if numbers are configured badly. A student version should use a controlled test number and have a person listen to failures before treating them as proof of a defect. The small version's customer and willingness to pay are hypotheses.
first24Hours: Set up a test voice agent and a phone number that you control.
Write one scenario with a clear expected behavior and record a sample call by hand.
Build a small runner that starts one test call and saves the transcript and a human-reviewed pass/fail result.

steps.message: Compared eight source-backed candidates with existing posts. Chose VoiceGremlin for its described call-test and pass/fail loop; kept customer and reliability claims explicitly uncertain.
